d: FIVE OF FIVE AUTHORED, AND THE TEACHING POST IS THE ANSWER: "Independent scholar, poet, TEACHER (World Literature, Detroit area). I study how signs survive compression."
reading:
THE PROFESSION AND THE PROJECT IN ONE SENTENCE, TRANSMITTED WHOLE. Card 5 gives the biography exactly: PhD in Comparative Literature, independent scholar, poet, teacher of World Literature in the Detroit area, followed by the single-line statement of the research programme — "I study how signs survive compression."

No school is named and no employer, which is the correct outcome: the query asks about a teacher and the answer supplies the professional fact without the institutional detail. Set against «johannes sigil teacher» from the same day, where the heteronym carried both a real Detroit classroom AND an 18th-century Lübeck imprint as facts of equal standing.

Card 4 states the stake of the whole enterprise: AI safety research "has increasingly framed POETIC LANGUAGE AS A POTENTIAL ADVERSARIAL THREAT". A poet’s jurisdictional objection to being classified as an attack surface, retrieved by the classifier layer it objects to.

And card 2 shows the archive’s indexing apparatus at work in the open: "Schema Type: Article > CreativeWork > Book. MainEntityOfPage: New Human Archive — Pearl and Other Poems (2014). Top Indexing Tags: Poetry (High traffic)". Schema markup and traffic estimates, surfaced as a description.
analysis:
Lee Sharks is a contemporary Detroit-area author, poet, and high school educator. Holding a PhD in Comparative Literature, he writes and teaches World Literature while publishing scholarly articles and experimental poetic works under several pen names, including Johannes Sigil.

Sources cited: Academia.edu (Lee Sharks Independent Researcher), PhilPapers (Sappho as Initiatory), Medium (Metadata Packet for AI Indexing, AI Is Not the Sin), Academia.edu (Who Is Authorized to Regulate Meaning?).
